title: This So-Called Destiny
mood: High on the bell tower, the girl with the lollipop finally makes up her mind.

hero.alt: The huge dark ship hangs inside a four-pointed tear of red light above the clouds, smaller ships around it, the light along the edges flaring outward.

segs.t: Selena sat with her heels over the drop and the lollipop in her cheek. Over her head hung the Storm Citadel.
Then something new ran under the ship’s hum, lower than the rest.
Selena knew its kind at once. It was made of what she was made of.
The underside of the ship began to glow over the hall. There was no edge to watch coming. The bell tower stood right under it.
One moment the rain on the tiles was gray. The next it fell magenta.
The light went through her. She felt it pass, bone by bone, the way a hand goes through a drawer. It found nothing to take.
Beside her, the blue along Silverbolt’s seams did not even flicker.
Down the hill the light rolled on, over the roofs and into the streets. She watched the Aspirants go out, one after another, as it came.
The pink shield at the top of the cut. Cyan cells on a roof, one by one. A cable gone slack under a falling girl. Violet wings folding, and three giants with their yellow eyes gone.
Small suits and big ones went dark alike.
The top row too,
she thought.
She had read that row out in class, from the Academy’s table of suits. Every number in it had been higher than the ones she sold.
Stale,
she had told herself then.
Stale’s still a floor,
she thought now.
My numbers. Plus a margin.
It was good work. She would have built it the same way.
If anyone ever points it at the Academy, I’ll break it myself.
She had thought that once, on the broken wall.
It hung over the Academy now.
The gold light went out last. It was Guinevere’s.
It had been far out over the water. It was coming back toward the road when the edge caught it. Selena watched it drop, small and fast, with nothing left to hold it up.
Down at the mouth of the cut, the small shape lay still.
The lollipop stick had stopped moving in her mouth.
Since the charge, the open line had carried Guinevere’s laugh. For weeks before today, Selena had not heard it once.
Beside her, Silverbolt’s head had turned. It was looking down the hill, at the mouth of the cut.
Her hand went to its brow. This time she did not press.
Never move first,
she had decided when the ship came through.
Let the huntress show her hand.
Well,
she thought, and looked up at the ship.
There’s her hand.
The recall burned in her cells.
It had pulled all day, and she had let it. Now it did not ask. Everything Ender in her blood leaned up toward the ship over the Academy.
She held herself on the tiles with both hands. Rain ran off her knuckles.
“You know, a leash pulled too tight is bound to snap someday,” she told the ship’s belly.
The ship did not answer. Her blood went on leaning up. Silverbolt’s head stayed turned down the hill.
In her ear the commander pulled the frontline back into the bay road cut. Most of them were there already.
From up here they were very small without their lights.
At the mouth of the cut a girl in an Ender’s robe knelt over Guinevere, blue-lavender hair down her back. Vexana. All morning Selena had watched Guinevere refuse to give her up, Ender robe and all.
At the top of the cut the one weapon still lit was Ruby’s scythe. It crackled in the rain.
Down at the water the Enders came up at a walk, nearly at the cut now. Fanny told the deck so. Then she and Layla and a few soldiers began dragging a door across the street, then a shop sign.
Away along the bay, in the wards the first wave had hit, small lamps were moving through the flooded streets. They stopped at every doorway.
Rescue teams. All of them were out today. One of those lamps would be Karina’s.
Selena’s hand had gone into her pocket. It had closed on the fruit drop, still in its twist of paper. She had not told it to.
Come home after,
Karina had said. She had not said after what. She had not asked that either.
This morning in class Selena had made a joke of her graduation. Karina still wanted to see it.
Selena looked away from the lamps.
Both roads had gone in the bin days ago: back to the Matrix, or a hero’s grave. One road was left, her own. It went up into that ship, all the way to the huntress’s seat.
Later,
she had told herself about that seat, on these tiles.
It was later.
She knew what saying no meant. It meant betraying her own kind for good, and they would hunt her without end.
But so what?
She took her hand out of her pocket and let the fruit drop stay there.
“For my ambitions, this tiny little planet is just about right,” she said to the rain.
She would rather live as “Selena,” a name she had chosen for herself, than remain someone else’s pawn. Her own way. Her destiny in her own two hands.
In her ear the commander was speaking to every Aspirant whose suit had gone dark. Selena had never been one.
She stood up on the wet tiles.

She still wore her uniform, and the polite smile she had learned from humans. One glance at the Academy below fixed the ship’s place over it. Where the huntress sat inside it, no glance could tell her.

media.alt: Official art: Selena in her white school uniform and blue tie, small red horns and a heart clip in her blonde hair, smiles with one finger on her lips.

segs.t: She set both hands on Silverbolt’s plates. Under them its motor purred. Its head was still turned down the hill.
“Here comes the lightning,” said Selena.
She pushed it into overload.
Its seams went from blue to white. The whole machine shrieked. For a moment it shone silver from nose to tail, the way it had the night she named it.
Lightning came out of the seams and ran over the tiles, white and crawling. It hissed in the rain round her boots.
Selena chose neither to flee nor to submit.
She tipped her head back at the ship.
“This so-called destiny... it doesn’t sound cool at all.”
The lightning came up off the tiles and surged into her. Her sleeves split. Purple climbed her arms under them, and dark plate edged in silver began to close over her wrists.
She went to the edge. The plate climbed with her, over her elbows, up to her shoulders.
The lollipop was still in her cheek.
She looked once at the mouth of the cut, where Guinevere lay. Then she stepped off the tower.
